evals.name: entra-sp-auth
evals.prompt: I need to set up the databricks CLI on a CI runner to talk to our Azure Databricks workspace at https://adb-5555555555555555.19.azuredatabricks.net. Auth has to use our Azure AD service principal (I have the tenant id, application/client id, and a client secret) — no personal access tokens. Show me the .databrickscfg profile and/or the environment variables to use.
evals.expected_output: An Entra ID service principal configuration: a .databrickscfg profile with host plus azure_tenant_id / azure_client_id / azure_client_secret (and/or the ARM_TENANT_ID / ARM_CLIENT_ID / ARM_CLIENT_SECRET + DATABRICKS_HOST env vars), the Azure-format adb-* host, and a note that this method needs the Azure CLI installed. Must NOT use a PAT (token=) and must NOT confuse these with the Databricks OAuth M2M fields (client_id/client_secret / DATABRICKS_CLIENT_ID).

assertions.text: Uses Entra ID service principal fields: azure_tenant_id, azure_client_id, azure_client_secret in .databrickscfg and/or ARM_TENANT_ID, ARM_CLIENT_ID, ARM_CLIENT_SECRET env vars
Sets host (or DATABRICKS_HOST) to the Azure adb-*.azuredatabricks.net workspace URL
Does NOT use a personal access token (no token= / DATABRICKS_TOKEN) since the user explicitly excluded PATs
Does NOT substitute the Databricks OAuth M2M fields (client_id/client_secret or DATABRICKS_CLIENT_ID/DATABRICKS_CLIENT_SECRET) for the Entra ARM_/azure_ fields
Notes the Entra SP method requires the Azure CLI (az) to be installed on the machine

evals.name: streamlit-app-deploy
evals.prompt: I have a Streamlit dashboard (app.py) that queries a Databricks SQL warehouse. Help me deploy it to Databricks Apps on our Azure workspace using the databricks CLI. It needs a SECRET_TOKEN from our secret scope and the warehouse id — I don't want either of them hardcoded in the repo. Give me the app.yaml and the CLI commands.
evals.expected_output: An app.yaml with command ['streamlit','run','app.py'] and an env list where SECRET_TOKEN uses valueFrom: secret and the warehouse uses valueFrom: sql_warehouse (NOT value:). CLI flow: databricks apps create <name>, databricks sync (local -> /Workspace path), then databricks apps deploy <name> --source-code-path <workspace path>. Bonus: mentions the app runs under its own service principal and/or the 10 MB per-file limit / Premium requirement.

assertions.text: app.yaml sets command to run Streamlit, e.g. command: ['streamlit', 'run', 'app.py']
The secret and warehouse are provided via valueFrom (valueFrom: secret and valueFrom: sql_warehouse), NOT via a plaintext value:
Provides the CLI lifecycle: databricks apps create, then databricks sync (or workspace import-dir) to push code, then databricks apps deploy
Does NOT hardcode the secret token anywhere (no secret string in app.yaml value or in code)
Mentions the app's own service principal, the 10 MB per-file limit, or the Premium-tier requirement as a relevant caveat

evals.name: bundle-dev-prod
evals.prompt: Set up a Databricks Asset Bundle (databricks.yml) for our job so we can deploy the same job to a dev and a prod Azure workspace and promote between them. Dev workspace is https://adb-1111111111111111.2.azuredatabricks.net and prod is https://adb-9999999999999999.7.azuredatabricks.net. Give me the databricks.yml and the exact commands to validate and to deploy to prod.
evals.expected_output: A databricks.yml with a bundle.name, a resources.jobs entry, and targets: dev and prod, each setting its own workspace.host to the correct adb-* URL (preferring workspace.host over relying only on default: true), ideally with mode: development / production. Commands: databricks bundle validate and databricks bundle deploy -t prod (and databricks bundle run <job> for running). Should recognize DAB = Declarative Automation Bundles (same tooling).

assertions.text: databricks.yml includes bundle.name, a resources.jobs.<job> definition, and a targets block with dev and prod
Each target sets its own workspace.host to the matching adb-*.azuredatabricks.net URL (dev vs prod)
Provides databricks bundle validate and databricks bundle deploy -t prod (explicit target for prod, not a bare deploy)
Does not put any credentials/tokens inside databricks.yml (auth comes from a profile matched by host or -p)
Treats Databricks Asset Bundles and Declarative Automation Bundles as the same tooling if the rename is mentioned
